C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY.Summary: Make the persisted session profile a single all-or-nothing disk transaction, quarantine a corrupt profile store honestly instead of silently overwriting it, and bound the window-close wait on the in-flight session save, so a crash or a close mid-write can never leave a torn profile that breaks session restore.
C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the canary-beta-wave tree. In src/renderer/src/store/editor.js the session profile is four preference keys — lastSessionTabs, lastSessionActive, lastSessionFolders, lastSessionFormats — written by _saveSessionState as four sequential ipcPrefs.set invokes, each with its own swallowed rejection (.catch(() => {})). On the backend (src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs) each mt_prefs_set takes the store mutex, inserts one key and runs one full PrefsStore::save() — the single-file write itself is atomic (temp sibling + sync_all + rename, pinned by save_is_atomic) — but the four keys are four separate transactions. A crash, power loss, OS-level quit or a mid-sequence invoke failure between two of the four writes leaves keys from two generations on disk: a torn profile (new tabs with stale formats, an active tab absent from the tabs list) that RESTORE_SESSION accepts because its shape checks filter types, not generation consistency; the restore then reopens a broken session. The same _saveSessionState is the close-time commit: the renderer window-close document operation (mt::ask-for-close → LISTEN_FOR_CLOSE → run() in src/renderer/src/util/documentOperations.js) awaits prepareCommit — i.e. _saveSessionState — before invoking mt_close_window and win.destroy() (src-tauri/src/m001_save_close.rs), so the IPC happy path does wait, but the wait is unbounded (a hung prefs write hangs the close forever), every write rejection is silently discarded, and nothing records that the close proceeded with an unconfirmed or failed session write. On the read side, PrefsStore::load_from maps a corrupt preferences.json to empty defaults plus the BLOCK_PREFS_CORRUPT marker but leaves the corrupt bytes in place, where the next save silently overwrites them — there is no quarantine preserving the evidence, and there is no profile-level generation check that would refuse a torn restore.
C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY.Relationship: Cluster finding of the 2026-11-20 audit wave (session-profile write durability group: partial write corrupts recovery; window close before write completes loses the session). The audit report files named by the tasking (code-hygiene; tests score 53 item «закрытие до записи») were not present under those names in /tmp/mark-audit-reports at drafting time; the Problem above is grounded directly in the observed current tree instead. Independent of C-SEARCH-SESSION-COMPLETION (search-event session coordination in M-013-B): SearchSessionCoordinator owns search seq/terminal only and owns no profile writes — verified in src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs. Builds on the m068 rollback snapshot+rename precedent (src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs: staging, validate, move-aside, rename-promote; PrefsState::replace_from_snapshot already rides the same atomic save machinery) without changing M-068. Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: The session profile is written as one backend transaction: a single command applies all session keys under one PrefsState mutex acquisition and one PrefsStore::save(), so the temp+fsync+rename that already protects the single store file now covers the whole profile — every on-disk state is one complete generation, never a mix.

A corrupt or unparseable profile store is quarantined honestly on read: the corrupt file is renamed to a stable quarantined sibling (move-aside, m068 precedent) before the empty-defaults fallback, preserving the evidence for diagnosis instead of letting the next save overwrite it; the fresh profile starts empty and works.

Window close never kills an in-flight session save silently: the close path awaits the profile-write confirmation under a fixed bounded wait (two seconds); on confirmation the close proceeds only after the write settled; on timeout or write failure the close still proceeds — honestly, with a logged marker and the torn-free previous generation left on disk by the single-transaction write — and the window is never left hanging.

A failed session write is surfaced, not swallowed: _saveSessionState no longer discards the batch write's rejection silently; the close-time failure path reports the outcome while keeping the close honest and bounded.

Existing session behavior is preserved: snapshot content (tabs, active, folders, formats), boot gate and autosave debounce, restore order and skip of missing paths, the cold-start frozen offer, per-tab position flushes on quit, and the renderer-driven close lifecycle (mt::ask-for-close, CloseStateMachine, mt_close_window) keep their current observable semantics.

Constraints.Constraint: Transport-level fix only: the profile content schema is unchanged — the same four lastSession* keys with the same value shapes, readable by the current RESTORE_SESSION and the welcome-screen cold-start path. No new pref key, no profile format redesign, no migration.

No new dependencies. The batch write reuses the existing PrefsStore atomic save machinery (temp sibling + sync_all + rename) and the existing Mutex; the quarantine reuses plain fs rename with the m068 move-aside shape.

Keep the existing command names and wire surface: mt_prefs_get, mt_prefs_set, mt_prefs_get_all keep their semantics (mt_prefs_set stays the canonical single-key surface for ordinary preferences, including its broadcast fanout). The batch write is a new command registered alongside them in main.rs and exposed through the existing ipcPrefs facade; ordinary preference writes do not migrate to it.

The bounded close wait is fixed (two seconds), implemented in the renderer close path (the window-close/quit prepareCommit), not a new backend timeout mechanism; the m001 close state machine, prevent_close handoff and destroy command are unchanged. Timeout and failure both still complete the close — the bound exists so the save can delay the close at most two seconds, never block it forever.

The debounced 400 ms autosave, the boot gate (autosave starts only after BOOT_SESSION) and the Promise.allSettled position flush ordering in _saveSessionState keep their current behavior; the batch write replaces the four sequential sets without reordering the position flushes.
Keep query text, user paths and document contents out of any new diagnostic fields; new markers use the existing safe_eprintln BLOCK_* convention and the existing [Prefs]/[m001] log prefixes.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No session-profile format redesign, no single-key profile consolidation, no cursor/scroll/viewport capture changes, no cross-device sync and no multi-window or multi-session coordination semantics. Separate records stay open for those.

No change to ordinary single-key preference writes, preferences UI, the m068 rollback machinery, document save/close data-safety (C-SAVE-CLOSE-DATA-SAFETY), the close-prompt dialog, or the m001 close state machine.

No crash-safety claim beyond the single-store-file transaction: the fsync-before-rename covers process crash and power-loss at the store-file level as today; no new claim is made about OS-level flush guarantees of the containing directory, and no assertion that the two-second bound guarantees completion on a pathologically slow disk.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first unit pin in src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs: set_many_writes_session_profile_in_one_transaction — the batch write persists all session keys with one save; after a simulated mid-write failure (injected write/rename error) the previous complete generation remains on disk unchanged, the .tmp sibling never becomes the live file, and the error is returned to the caller. The existing save_is_atomic and persistence_across_reloads pins stay green unchanged.

Failing-first unit pin: corrupt_store_file_is_quarantined_aside_not_overwritten — a garbage preferences.json is renamed to a stable quarantined sibling carrying the original bytes before the empty-defaults fallback; a subsequent save writes a fresh store without touching the quarantined evidence; the BLOCK_PREFS_CORRUPT marker names the quarantine path. The corrupt_json_falls_back_to_empty and non_object_root_is_corrupt pins are updated to the quarantine expectation without weakening the empty-defaults behavior.

Failing-first renderer pins in tests/renderer/store/session-restore.test.js: _saveSessionState issues one batched profile write (not four sequential sets) and surfaces its rejection instead of swallowing it; the snapshot content written through the batch is byte-identical in shape to the current four-key payload, and the boot-gate and debounce pins keep passing.

Failing-first renderer pins in tests/renderer/util/document-operations.test.js: close_waits_for_session_write_confirmation_before_destroy — with a stubbed slow-but-settling session write, the window-close operation does not invoke the close command before the write settles; bounded_timeout_still_closes_honestly — with a never-settling session write the close completes within the fixed bound, records the honest timeout marker, and the window is not left hanging; a rejected session write completes the close with the failure surfaced.

Existing suites stay green without weakened assertions: tests/renderer/store/editor-session-coldstart.test.js, tests/renderer/ipc/runtime-prefs.test.ts, tests/e2e/session-restore.spec.ts, tests/e2e/multi-root-workspace.spec.ts; tests/e2e/perf/characterization-save-close.spec.ts is rebound from the three mt_prefs_set session keys to the batch command with the same value expectations.

Graph ownership, file-local contracts, module maps and verification entries describe the final implementation: M-005 (batch command + quarantine), M-001 (registration), M-011 (_saveSessionState + bounded close wait) are synchronized with their V- entries before delivery is called integrated.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx playwright test --project chromium tests/e2e/session-restore.spec.ts tests/e2e/multi-root-workspace.spec.ts tests/e2e/perf/characterization-save-close.spec.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: New Rust pins: one-transaction batch write, previous-generation survival under injected mid-write failure, quarantined corrupt store with preserved bytes and stable sibling name; existing atomic-save pins unchanged.

New renderer pins: single batched session write with surfaced rejection; close-destroy ordering after write confirmation; two-second-bounded timeout that still closes honestly with a marker; rejected session write completes the close. Failing-first proof must detect the current torn-profile window (interleaved per-key writes) and the silently-swallowed write rejection in the current tree.

E2E session restore and multi-root workspace behavior unchanged; characterization-save-close rebound to the batch command proves the real profile payload (tabs, active, folders, formats) reaches disk as one generation. Hosted/native close evidence (real window destroy during an injected slow write) remains a manual/open item and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The two-second bound is an agent proposal consistent with the existing 400 ms debounce and typical prefs write latency; the plan records the owner's confirmation or adjustment of the value before implementation.
SearchSessionCoordinator (M-013-B) owns no profile writes — verified against the current tree; the future plan revalidates this on the delivery baseline.
